title: SF2E Common Definitions
description: Shared building blocks for representing Starfinder Second Edition mechanics, referenced via $ref by kid.schema.json, frame.schema.json, creature.schema.json, npc.schema.json, subsystem.schema.json, and challenge.schema.json. Grounded against reference/srd/ (Player Core Ch.4/6/7/8, GM Core creature-building and encounter chapters). Not an entity schema itself — nothing is stored directly in this shape.

proficiencyRank.description: Untrained = +0 flat (does not scale with level). Trained = level+2, Expert = level+4, Master = level+6, Legendary = level+8. Expert requires no minimum level; Master requires level 7+; Legendary requires level 15+ (Player Core Ch.4).

proficiency.description: A single proficiency-gated statistic (a save, Perception, a skill, Class DC, spell DC/attack, weapon/armor category).

modifier.description: Final computed bonus ready to use in a roll: proficiency bonus + relevant attribute modifier + item/other permanent bonuses. Store the computed total rather than requiring re-derivation.

abilityModifiers.description: The six attribute modifiers. SF2E represents attributes as modifiers only (Player Core Ch.4) — there is no separate underlying score to track.

riders.description: Rare save-wide bonuses, e.g. "+1 status bonus to all saves vs. magic."

skillName.description: The 18 fixed-name skills (Player Core Ch.4). Lore is excluded here — it's a repeatable, player-named skill; see the `lore` array alongside `skills`.

skills.description: Map of the 18 fixed skills to their proficiency, plus a separate array for named Lore skills (a character can hold several, e.g. "Starfinder Lore").

specialUses.description: Situational skill modifiers that differ from the base entry, e.g. "Athletics +7 (+9 to Climb or Grab)" on a creature statblock.

name.description: e.g. darkvision, low-light vision, scent, magnetic scent.

speed.description: All values in feet. GM Core creature-building: penalties floor at 5 ft.

hover.description: Qualifier on fly Speed, not a separate movement type.

dice.description: e.g. "2d12". Omit for a flat bonus-only or condition-only effect (e.g. a pure persistent-damage rider).

persistent.description: True if this is persistent damage rather than instantaneous.

traits.description: e.g. agile, finesse, reach, thrown, deadly. Weapon-trait bonuses are pre-folded into attackBonus/damage; traits are kept as strings because some conditions (clumsy, enfeebled) key off specific trait names.

reach.description: Feet. Melee only; normally derived from size but can be overridden by a trait.

damage.description: First entry is the base damage; further entries are additional/rider damage (e.g. +1d6 fire from an upgrade).

name.description: A damage type, a condition, or an effect-trait (e.g. "death effects", "disease", "mental"), or the special tags "critical hits" / "nonlethal".

duration.description: Only for temporary immunities, e.g. "1 minute".

condition.description: Full condition list per Player Core Conditions Appendix (reference/srd/player-core/425-effects.json / 504-conditions-appendix.json).

activeCondition.description: A condition currently applied to a character/creature in play (session state, not a fixed sheet field).

value.description: For valued conditions: dying, wounded, doomed, clumsy, enfeebled, drained, stupefied, sickened, slowed, stunned, etc. all take a numeric value.

actionCost.description: variable covers abilities like Piloting's Drive, listed as "[one-action] to [three-actions]".

ability.description: A special/reactive ability, class feature action, or similar named capability. Shape generalized from the Reactive Step worked example (Player Core pg. 130) and GM Core's ability-design categories (Active/Free/Reactions/Constant-Automatic/Skill Abilities).

bulk.description: 0 = negligible, 0.1 = light (10 light items = 1 Bulk), integers otherwise.

integrated.description: Can't be Disarmed/looted while the creature lives (creature stat blocks); recharges over 24 hours.

creatureTraits.description: Ordered per GM Core convention: [rarity trait if not common] → [size] → [remaining traits, alphabetical]. Common categories: creature type (aberration/animal/beast/construct/humanoid/undead/etc.), holy/unholy (SF2E's replacement for a good/evil axis), elemental/energy affinity, and mechanically-detailed tags (amphibious, incorporeal, mindless, swarm).

degreeOfSuccessOutcome.description: Not all four degrees need be specified — SF2E subsystem/spell text often only defines 2-3 and leaves the rest as "no effect" by omission.

dc.description: DC-setting is rarely a bare number in practice — it's a level/proficiency-derived base plus situational adjustments (see reference/tables/dc-and-check-math.json for the underlying tables).

value.description: The final DC to roll against.

basis.description: How it was derived, e.g. "level 7 DC", "NPC Will-based social DC".

check.description: One atomic DC'd check — the building block for challenge.schema.json and subsystem.schema.json obstacles/tasks.

skillOptions.description: One or more skills/saves/Perception that can be used, e.g. ["stealth", "society"]. List low-DC-to-high-DC if they differ in difficulty.

secret.description: GM rolls, doesn't reveal the degree of success to the player.

pcArmorClass.description: AC as derived on a PC sheet (Player Core: 10 + Dex mod, capped by armor's Dex cap, + armor proficiency + armor item bonus + other bonuses). Creature stat blocks instead just author a flat AC integer — see creature.schema.json.

pcStatblock.description: The full SF2E player-character sheet shape (Player Core Ch.1-8), shared by kid.schema.json and frame.schema.json — both are built as complete, standard SF2E PCs (design bible: 'Pick a class, build it exactly as any level-12 PC'). Gaps intentionally left flexible rather than hardcoded: per-class feat/skill-increase cadence and spell-slot progression vary by class, so they're recorded per-character (via levelGained on each feat/feature, and the slots array) rather than assumed from a universal table.

xp.description: Rolls over at 1000 (level up, remainder carries).

heritage.description: Versatile heritages can attach to any ancestry, so this isn't strictly a child of ancestry.

size.description: Derived from ancestry for a kid; a Frame's fiction-layer size is separate from this mechanical value.

abilities.description: Granted actions/reactions/free actions beyond core class features, e.g. from feats or equipment.

activeConditions.description: Session state, not a fixed sheet field.

combatStatblock.description: The full SF2E monster/NPC stat block shape (GM Core creature-building rules), excluding identity fields (id/type/name) so it can be embedded (e.g. npc.schema.json's optional `statblock`) as well as used standalone (creature.schema.json). Distinct from pcStatblock: flat authored AC/skills instead of derived-from-proficiency, no ancestry/background/leveling chargen fields.

nonCombatLevel.description: Optional separate level for non-combat challenges (GM Core example: a corporate lawyer might be level -1 in combat but 4th-level in legal matters). Non-combat XP uses this instead of level.

adjustment.description: GM Core: adjustments shift level by 1 and should be applied at most once; work best on physical-combat-focused creatures. No numeric delta table survived in the mirrored SRD text as of the last check — treat any elite/weak deltas as GM judgment calls, not verified rule numbers, until reference material confirms them.

baseCreatureRef.description: id of the un-adjusted creature/NPC this is an elite/weak version of, if adjustment is set.

languages.description: Can include non-language communication modes (telepathy, truespeech, envisioning). "none" is valid.

ac.description: Flat authored value (unlike a PC's derived AC).

abilities.description: Special/reactive abilities: active, free-action, reaction, constant/automatic, and skill abilities per GM Core's ability-design categories.

profileRef.description: Design doc §50 (Archetype Ladder Stage E) — OPTIONAL, battle-simulator-tooling-only. Unlike every other *Ref field in this schema, this does NOT point at another /data JSON file: it's the id of a real, already-tested AI profile object defined in tools/battle-simulator/personnel-engine/ai-profiles.mjs (BASELINE_V1, NO_MANEUVERS_V1) or archetypes.mjs (aggressive-v1/cautious-v1/flanker-v1/brawler-v1/mindless-v1/zealot-v1 — ALL_PROFILES is the live, authoritative registry; check there for the current real list, since new archetypes are expected to be added over time and this description will not be kept in lockstep). Deliberately NOT an enum: the profile's own real numbers (weights, competence, templates...) belong in exactly one place — the JS module that's already built, tested, and battle-verified — duplicating them into campaign JSON here would just be a second copy that could silently drift from the real one, the same 'frozen in name only' risk ai-profiles.mjs's own header already warns about for a DIFFERENT reason. Purely descriptive metadata for a human (or a future encounter-validation tool) to know 'when this creature needs to fight in the simulator, play it like THIS' — never read by the Foundry sync pipeline, which has no concept of AI weights at all.
